judgments.reason: The passage establishes a special commission to study and define conditions for legalizing single-stair multi-family residential buildings up to six stories in Massachusetts.
The passage states the commission shall produce a building code amendment allowing such buildings, including measures mitigating health and safety impacts.
The passage names a technical safety study comparing single-stair to two-staircase buildings plus a process map and timeline for implementation.
The listed measures—smoke alarms, sprinkler systems, fire-resistant materials, and emergency exit strategies—appear verbatim in the passage.
The passage says the study shall build on the named report produced by those three organizations.
The passage designates the secretary of housing and livable communities or their designee as chair.
Each category named in the claim corresponds to a membership slot listed in the passage.
The listed interests all hold seats on the commission per the passage, and the drafting role is consistent with the bill's commission.
The passage sets the filing deadline of July 31, 2026 for the commission's study, with no added detail in the claim.
